subject: BlueWave: follow-up on runtime fit and latency/throughput requirements
messages:
From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sims <emily.sims@bluewavehealth.com>, Roy Chen <roy.chen@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-22T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Recap & quick asks after today's discovery call

Hi Emily / Roy —

Thanks for the time today. Quick recap and the information we'll need to recommend the right deployment path (Hosted API vs Dedicated vs Private VPC):

What we heard from BlueWave:
- Primary use: contextual summarization + assisted charting for clinician notes (long prompts + multi-turn).
- Latency sensitivity: interactive UI needs sub-500ms tail; key target you mentioned was p95 ~220ms and p99 under ~450ms.
- Traffic profile: baseline ~25 RPS (steady), expected daily peaks up to ~140 RPS for ~5-15 minute windows during shift changes.
- Typical prompt size: average ~350 tokens, occasional up to ~1,200 tokens.
- Compliance: SOC 2 is required; initial pilot can run on Hosted while we evaluate Private options.

Open asks for us to size and recommend:
1) Can you share a small sample of representative prompt payloads and the distribution by token length? (CSV or sample JSON fine)
2) Confirm the sustained peak window length and whether peaks repeat multiple times per hour/day.
3) Any hard limit on p99 latency vs preference? You called out 450ms as a target — is that a hard SLO for go-live?

Recommended next steps (high level):
- If p99 < 450ms is a hard requirement for production and peaks are sustained (tens of minutes), Dedicated reserved capacity is the safer path for predictable tail latency.
- For an initial validation we can run a short Hosted test using your sample payloads to prove correctness and get a first-pass latency profile; if that shows tight tail behavior we'd propose a 30-day Dedicated pilot (reserved pool with autoscale/burst policy) to validate under real traffic.
- For teams that are OK with slightly higher variance on the tail, Hosted + adaptive routing (fallback to a larger model or region) can reduce cost and time-to-value.

I've attached a short checklist for sample artifacts if you have them handy (throughput profile, sample payloads).

Attachments: BlueWave_Throughput_Profile.csv (if available)

Would you prefer we schedule a 30-minute technical pilot planning call with Priyom (solutions) and Marissa (sales) to lock the test windows and acceptance criteria?

Thanks —
Sofia
Sofia Ivanova

Subject: Re: Recap & quick asks after today's discovery call

Thanks Sofia — helpful recap. A few clarifications from our side:  

- Prompt distribution: average ~350 tokens, 90th percentile ~850 tokens, max ~1200 tokens. I'll attach the throughput CSV (shows hourly spikes over the last 7 days).
- Peak behavior: spikes correlate with shift changes and billing batches — typically 2–3 spikes/day, each roughly 8–12 minutes long. We saw one anomalous 20-minute spike last week.
- Latency SLO: p95 = 220ms is the business target; p99 < 450ms is our go/no-go for the pilot to be meaningful. We can be flexible for a short pilot, but production must meet the p99 target.
- Compliance: SOC 2 Type II evidence is needed for vendor selection; we have a legal review timeline next month. For the pilot we are OK with Hosted if SOC docs are provided.

Quick Qs:  
1) Ballpark cost: do you have a rough monthly delta between Hosted versus Dedicated for the level described?
2) Does Dedicated support automatic scale-up for short bursts, or do we need to provision headroom?

Attachment: BlueWave_Throughput_Profile.csv

—Emily

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia.ivanova@redwood.com>
To: Emily Sims <emily.sims@bluewavehealth.com>, Roy Chen <roy.chen@bluewavehealth.com>
Cc: Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>, Lauren Bishop <lauren.bishop@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-08-24T11:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Recap & quick asks after today's discovery call

Emily — thanks for the file and the clarifications, that helps a lot. Summary below and specific recommendations based on the numbers you shared.

Short answers to your Qs:
- Ballpark cost: for steady-state throughput at ~25 RPS with the occasional burst profile you shared, Hosted monthly would typically be lower for initial months (pay-as-you-go). Dedicated becomes cost-effective when sustained throughput / predictable peaks exceed our hosted pooling economics — ballpark delta ~20–40% higher monthly committed cost but with 2–4x better tail stability (depends on model size and quantization). We'll provide a tailored quote after we pick the model config.
- Dedicated autoscale: Dedicated supports policy-driven autoscale and burst capacity. Short bursts (<= a few minutes) are best handled with an allocated burst pool; autoscale can grow the pool but there is non-zero warm-up for large capacity. For your short 8–12 minute spikes we recommend a modest burst reserve to avoid warm starts.

Recommendation (based on p99 < 450ms requirement + peak profile):
- Pilot recommendation: 30-day Dedicated reserved pilot with a small burst pool plus automatic fallback to Hosted in case of overflow. This gives predictability for p99 while keeping overall cost measured.
- Pilot acceptance criteria: p95 <= 250ms and p99 <= 450ms for representative synthetic load using your sample payloads and a 15-minute sustained peak at 140 RPS.
- Test artifacts we need from BlueWave: sample payloads, a list of representative sessions (for multi-turn), and the throughput CSV (you already provided — thank you).

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) will run a 2-hour synthetic validation on Hosted using your sample payloads to surface any prompt-related latency outliers. This is low-friction and helps narrow model/config choices.
2) If validation looks promising, we prepare a 30-day Dedicated pilot SOW (attached draft) that includes burst pool sizing and acceptance criteria.
3) Exchange SOC 2 evidence and schedule legal review in parallel.

Attachments: redwood_inference-latency-sla.pdf, SOW-draft-BW.docx

Can we lock a pilot planning call on Monday morning PT? Priyom and Marissa will join to size the pilot and confirm the acceptance test.

Best —
Sofia

Internal notes (please treat as internal):

Quick plan based on Sofia/Emily thread above:
- Priority: size Dedicated reserved pool for 140 RPS sustained 15-minute window, average prompt 350 tokens, p99 target 450ms. Assume model = 13B quantized (we'll finalize after the hosted validation).
- Action items:
  * Marissa: confirm commercial terms / target start date with BlueWave (ETA 10 business days for SOW sign).
  * Sofia: run the 2-hour hosted synthetic test once BlueWave shares sample payloads and confirm p95/p99 numbers (helpful for right-sizing).
  * Me (Priyom): prepare pilot config (GPU count estimate, burst pool size, autoscale rules) and a quick internal cost delta (Committed vs Hosted) for the pilot.
  * Lauren: flag CS/Onboarding for dedicated deployment steps and SOC 2 artifact handoff.

Notes on risks: warm-up for autoscale could push p99 above target during the first 3–5 minutes of a large spike — plan to use a small burst reserve. Also monitor KV cache hit rates; for multi-turn clinician sessions cache hit helps reduce tail.

I'll draft a short runbook and share before the planning call.
